title: Berkshire 1992 letter: good businesses at fair prices, margin of safety, and the cost of float
summary: Buffett's 1992 letter covers value versus growth, the Williams discounted-cash-flow equation, margin of safety, acquisition discipline, the cost of insurance float, super-cat underwriting, stock option accounting, and low corporate overhead. He also accepts volatility for long-term returns and rejects market forecasting.

principles.text: Buy good businesses at fair prices rather than fair businesses at good prices.
principles.quote: And thereafter I revised my strategy and tried to buy good businesses at fair prices rather than fair businesses at good prices.

principles.text: Value and growth are joined at the hip; investing means paying no more than calculated value.
principles.quote: Growth is always a component in the calculation of value, constituting a variable whose importance can range from negligible to enormous and whose impact can be negative as well as positive.

principles.text: Growth only helps when each dollar invested creates over a dollar of long-term market value.
principles.quote: Growth benefits investors only when the business in point can invest at incremental returns that are enticing - in other words, only when each dollar used to finance the growth creates over a dollar of long-term market value.

principles.text: Insist on a margin of safety, and stay within businesses simple enough to understand.
principles.quote: We believe this margin-of-safety principle, so strongly emphasized by Ben Graham, to be the cornerstone of investment success.

principles.text: Success in investing comes from realistically defining what you don't know and avoiding big mistakes.
principles.quote: What counts for most people in investing is not how much they know, but rather how realistically they define what they don't know. An investor needs to do very few things right as long as he or she avoids big mistakes.

principles.text: Insurance float is only worth having if its cost beats the government's long-term bond rate.
principles.quote: (If, on average, we didn't beat the Government's rate, there would be no economic reason for us to be in the business.)
